claims.claim: The Supreme Court said a missing train ticket cannot defeat a compensation claim and restored the award to Maheshbhai's parents.
claims.episode_span: The Supreme Court said the failure to recover a train ticket from a dead passenger cannot defeat a compensation claim, and it restored the award to the parents of Maheshbhai.
claims.source_title: Non-recovery of train ticket from deceased passenger can't defeat compensation claim: Supreme Court
claims.supporting_quote: The Supreme Court has said the absence of recovery of a train ticket from a deceased passenger cannot result in defeating the compensation claim, as it restored the payout awarded to the parents of a man who died after falling from a moving train in Gujarat in 2017.

claims.claim: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A. S. Chandurkar set aside the Gujarat High Court order rejecting the compensation.
claims.episode_span: A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A. S. Chandurkar set aside a Gujarat High Court order that had rejected the payout.
claims.source_title: Non-recovery of train ticket from deceased passenger can't defeat compensation claim: Supreme Court
claims.supporting_quote: A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A.S. Chandurkar set aside the order of the Gujarat High Court rejecting the compensation awarded to the parents of Maheshbhai, who died falling off the general compartment following a sudden jerk and jolt while travelling to Surat via Ahmedabad on September 27, 2017.

claims.claim: Maheshbhai fell on 27 September 2017, was hospitalised for more than a month, and died on 31 October 2017.
claims.episode_span: Maheshbhai fell from a general compartment after a sudden jerk on 27 September 2017 while travelling to Surat via Ahmedabad, was hospitalised for more than a month, and died on 31 October 2017.
claims.source_title: Non-recovery of train ticket from deceased passenger can't defeat compensation claim: Supreme Court
claims.supporting_quote: He, however, succumbed to his injuries on October 31, 2017.

claims.claim: On 17 June 2022 the Railways Claim Tribunal awarded 8 lakh rupees with nine per cent interest a year from the incident until the tribunal order.
claims.episode_span: On 17 June 2022 the Railways Claim Tribunal held that the fall was an untoward incident and awarded his parents ₹8 lakh with interest at nine per cent a year from the date of the incident until the date of that order.
claims.source_title: Non-recovery of train ticket from deceased passenger can't defeat compensation claim: Supreme Court
claims.supporting_quote: On June 17, 2022, the Railways Claim Tribunal held that Maheshbhai was the victim of an 'untoward incident' and suffered an accidental fall, and his parents, who are the claimants, were held entitled to compensation of ₹8 lakh along with interest at the rate of nine per cent per annum from the date of the incident till the date of the order.
